answer: Because the custody account is separate, an attacker cannot recycle one pool of capital across 171 aliases, and each one needs its own funded copper account. Deposits are visible in nebula, and reef reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 16% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. That bill is paid per identity, so 293 aliases cost 348 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
